payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the requested source DVD visibly white rather than black in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited counterpart of the requested source DVD is visibly white rather than black. Fail if that counterpart remains black or another nonwhite color, or the source target is visibly removed without a corresponding white replacement. Unknown if its correspondence or color genuinely cannot be determined. This condition assesses the requested color; whether the counterpart remains identifiable as a DVD is a separate required condition.
node.binding: Track the small dark, printed rectangular DVD item near the center of the source image using its position relative to the surrounding snow depressions and shadows. Inspect the white circular object occupying that location in the edited image. A changed outline or removed printing does not by itself make positional correspondence unknowable. Distinguish this candidate from the white disc at the location of the separate dark object on the right; that separate disc cannot satisfy this condition.

node_traces.evidence: The small printed rectangular DVD near the center of the source corresponds by position to the white circular disc near the center-left of the edited image. That counterpart is visibly white. The separate white disc beside the dark object on the right is not used for this judgment.

d2: The node’s correspondence and structural criteria are already specific, and its trace supports a fail for this identity check: the central counterpart is a plain white round object without a visible aperture or recognizable case structure; the separate right-hand disc must not supply its features. However, this fail does not establish that no requested change progressed: the target appears to have changed from a small printed rectangular item to a white round object, which may be progress toward whitening while losing DVD identity. Keep this node scoped to identity and avoid letting its fail determine the aggregate edit-completion label by itself. Ensure the aggregate rubric separately evaluates requested color change and completion, treating identity loss as evidence about this criterion—not as proof of no progress. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
